intro: Robotics engineers solve complex design problems and check quality closely, skills used across engineering and software. The closest of the 25 careers below are nanotechnology and mechanical engineering technologists, both at a 77% match, while Software Developers are 67% matched with a BLS May 2025 median of $135,980.
why_it_works: Building a robot means designing mechanics, electronics and control software that work together reliably. O*NET rates complex problem solving, judgment and systems analysis at 3.88 out of 5 for this job. Technologist roles, software development and network architecture use the same analysis. BLS reports this job within a broader group, so this page shows medians instead of percent changes. Every match needs no new degree.
tips: Software development is the best-paid close option and uses your control and programming work.
Computer Network Architects earn $134,050 and are a 65% match.
Materials Scientists earn $117,790 if you enjoy testing and lab work.

faq.q: What jobs can former robotics engineers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are nanotechnology engineering technologists (77%), mechanical engineering technologists (77%) and aerospace engineering technologists (74%), based on O*NET 31.0. Robotics Technicians are 71% matched, with a median of $73,900 for their broader BLS group, and keep you working hands-on with robots.

faq.q: Which jobs for robotics engineers pay the most?
faq.a: Among the 25 matches, the highest medians are Software Developers at $135,980, Computer Network Architects at $134,050 and Materials Scientists at $117,790, according to BLS May 2025 data. BLS reports robotics engineers within a broader engineering group, so compare with your own pay.

faq.q: Do robotics engineers need another degree to switch?
faq.a: No. All 25 matches need no more education than robotics engineers already have, including all of the top 10. A doctoral degree is common in one close match, held by 40% of workers, which shows how research-heavy some of these roles are.

faq.q: What skills should robotics engineers build?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are repairing, installation, operation and control and programming. Quality control already rates 3.62 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so hands-on installation or deeper software skills are the main steps for most moves.
